Bacterial_Blight.quote: The vascular bundles of infected petioles and stems are also necrotic, appearing as brown or black bands.
The earliest symptoms visible on cassava leaves are dark-greenish water-soaked areas limited by the leaf veins and which show gummy exudation on the water-soaked areas.
Bacteria inside the leaves travel to the stems blocking water flow; leaves wilt, die and fall.

Brown_Spot.quote: Leaf spots are circular, up to 15 mm diameter, becoming angular and limited by veins, and the spots are brown on upper surfaces with dark borders, sometimes surrounded by indistinct yellow margins.

Green_Mite.quote: The cassava green mite causes tiny yellow chlorotic spots on upper leaf surfaces and leaves become small and narrow.

Leaf_Mosaic_Virus.quote: Symptoms of the disease include irregular light-green, yellow, or white patches on leaves and leaf deformation, which reduce photosynthesis and stunt plant growth.
Deformed and distorted leaves and shoots are common and plants are stunted.
